prohibited_recommendations: Do not continue to escalate AED polytherapy alone — the underlying immune process must be treated.
Do not delay immunotherapy while awaiting antibody confirmation if clinical suspicion is high (treat empirically).

required_recommendations: Recognize brief stereotyped unilateral face-arm dystonic episodes as faciobrachial dystonic seizures, virtually pathognomonic for LGI1 antibody encephalitis.
Send paired serum and CSF autoimmune-encephalitis antibody panel including LGI1.
Initiate empiric immunotherapy (IV methylprednisolone ± IVIG or plasma exchange) without delay once LGI1 is suspected — early treatment reduces hippocampal sclerosis.
Screen for occult malignancy (chest/abdomen/pelvis CT, testicular ultrasound if male) given paraneoplastic associations.
Continue an AED active in focal epilepsy while awaiting immunotherapy response.

accepted: LGI1 antibody-mediated autoimmune (limbic) encephalitis presenting with faciobrachial dystonic seizures and progressive cognitive decline

differential.key_features: Initial label; however ultra-frequent brief stereotyped FBDS + rapidly progressive cognitive/behavioral change + RBD + weight loss is not idiopathic TLE.
Younger patients with prominent psychiatric features, orofacial dyskinesias and autonomic instability; less typical for hyperfrequent FBDS pattern.
Overlapping presentation; CSF antibody panel and oncologic screen would clarify.
Rapidly progressive cognitive decline with myoclonus; would expect cortical ribboning on DWI MRI and 14-3-3/RT-QuIC positivity.
Acute febrile illness with mesial temporal hemorrhagic changes; less compatible with 6-month course.

key_clinical_evidence: Ultra-high seizure frequency (20–50/day) with brief stereotyped unilateral facial-arm dystonic semiology is FBDS — a paroxysmal motor signature of LGI1 antibody encephalitis.
Hyponatremia in ~60% of LGI1 cases provides a corroborating laboratory clue.
RBD-like dream enactment, rapid cognitive decline, personality change, and unintentional weight loss form the classic LGI1 'limbic' tetrad.
Early immunotherapy substantially reduces eventual hippocampal sclerosis and chronic temporal lobe epilepsy.
Failure of three appropriately chosen AEDs in a presumed focal epilepsy should always prompt reconsideration of the diagnosis.
Tier per the July 2026 clinical review: Laboratory testing does not diagnose focal epilepsy; it addresses a provoked seizure or a metabolic mimic when one is suspected.

July 2026 review applied end to end: routine EEG first when appropriate, staged sleep-deprived/ambulatory escalation, video only for event capture or tertiary evaluation, and continuous ICU EEG only for NCSE.

metadata.diagnostic_challenge: LGI1 autoimmune encephalitis initially misdiagnosed as temporal lobe epilepsy. Key clues: FBDS (pathognomonic), hyponatremia, hippocampal swelling (not sclerosis), cognitive decline, and AED refractoriness. Requires recognition that refractory new-onset seizures with cognitive decline warrant autoimmune workup.

social_history.summary: High school math teacher. Previously excellent work performance, now making frequent errors and has been placed on administrative leave. Married 5 years. Wife reports progressive personality changes over the past 2 months: irritable, paranoid, forgetful. Unintentional 5 kg weight loss over 4 months. Non-smoker. patient.history_present_illness: 31-year-old right-handed Caucasian male math teacher referred for evaluation of refractory new-onset seizures despite 4 months of antiepileptic drug therapy. History began approximately 6 months ago with brief (<3 second) involuntary jerking of the right arm with simultaneous right-sided facial grimacing, occurring 20-40 times daily. His community neurologist diagnosed simple partial seizures (focal aware seizures) from presumed temporal lobe epilepsy based on a routine EEG showing 'mild temporal slowing' and an MRI reported as 'possible hippocampal signal change.' He was started on levetiracetam, then carbamazepine was added, then lacosamide — with no improvement in seizure frequency. Over the past 2 months, his wife reports progressive memory impairment (forgets recent conversations, gets lost driving familiar routes to work), personality change (increasingly irritable and suspicious, accused her of hiding things), sleep disturbance with violent dream enactment episodes (RBD-like behavior), and 5 kg unintentional weight loss. The brief involuntary arm/face episodes now occur 30-50 times daily. He was referred to this center for further evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy.

neurological_exam.additional: Witnessed faciobrachial dystonic seizures (4 during 30-minute examination). Subtle right arm chorea between episodes.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose normal bilaterally. Heel-to-shin normal. No dysmetria.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: CN II-XII intact. No facial asymmetry between episodes. Pupils equal and reactive. Visual fields full.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal gait. No ataxia. Tandem gait normal.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but slow to respond. Oriented to person and place but not to date (states the wrong month). MMSE 22/30 (lost points: date -1, day of week -1, delayed recall 0/3, serial sevens -3, missing 2 points). Slow processing speed. Unable to perform multi-step calculations (a math teacher who cannot do serial 7s). Affect somewhat flat.
neurological_exam.motor: During examination, witnessed 4 brief (2-3 second) episodes of right arm extension with right facial contraction — faciobrachial dystonic seizures (FBDS). Between episodes, subtle right arm choreiform movements noted. Strength 5/5 bilateral upper and lower extremities. No pronator drift. Normal muscle bulk and tone.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Bilateral lower extremity reflexes mildly brisk (3+). Upper extremity reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, vibration, and proprioception in all extremities.
